name: Jeep Wrangler
evaluation_notes: JL generation only (2018+). Buyer wants a fun, reliable occasional overlanding vehicle — not a daily driver, not a project. Clean title essential. Sweet spot: 2018–2022, 30k–90k miles, $20k–$32k. Reward: factory Rubicon trim (locking diffs, sway bar disconnect), documented service history, low miles for year. Penalize: heavily lifted examples (suspension stress, alignment wear), evidence of off-road abuse without maintenance, near-MSRP pricing on recent model years. Flag: death wobble mentions, soft top damage, rust on tub floor or rockers. Sahara trim is the comfort/capability balance. Sport/Sport S is base — price should reflect it.

name: Jeep Renegade Trailhawk
evaluation_notes: Trailhawk trim only — must have Active Drive Low 4WD, skid plates, and hill descent. Buyer wants a fun, compact occasional vehicle that's easy to store and maintain. 2.4L naturally aspirated engine strongly preferred over 1.4T turbo (more reliable, fewer issues). 2017+ avoids worst 9-speed transmission bugs. Sweet spot: 2018–2022, under 70k miles, $12k–$18k. Reward: 2.4L engine, clean service history, low miles. Penalize: 1.4T turbo engine (more maintenance risk), high mileage, any transmission hesitation mentions. Flag: 9-speed transmission complaints, CVT mentions, rust on underbody, flood history.

name: Toyota 4Runner
evaluation_notes: 5th gen only (2014+). Buyer wants reliability above all — this is the most bulletproof option on the list. TRD Off Road or TRD Pro trim preferred (KDSS suspension, locking rear diff). SR5 is fine for occasional trail use. Sweet spot: 2015–2020, 50k–120k miles, $22k–$35k. Reward: TRD Off Road/Pro trim, documented Toyota dealer service history, KDSS equipped. Penalize: near-MSRP on recent years (buyer is not shopping new), SR5 without 4WD, high mileage above 130k. Note: timing chain not belt, head gaskets not an issue on 1GR-FE — these run forever with basic maintenance.

name: Lexus GX460
evaluation_notes: 2014+ only (post-interior refresh). Same platform and 4.6L V8 as 4Runner but with luxury interior and KDSS standard — excellent off-road capability with a comfortable cabin. Best value luxury overlander on the market. Sweet spot: 2015–2019, 50k–110k miles, $20k–$32k. Reward: low miles for year, full service history, KDSS equipped (all 2014+), Premium trim or above. Penalize: accident history (check Carfax), near-MSRP on recent years, deferred maintenance signs. Note: timing chain not belt, extremely reliable drivetrain. 2017+ shows best depreciation curve.
